insights.title: RUN GAME EDGE
insights.short: UGA run O #1 vs MISS run D #57; pass O #4 vs pass D #38.
insights.text: Georgia’s run offense (#1 of 138) faces Ole Miss’ run defense (#57 of 138): a clear measured gap, in Georgia’s favour. Through the air, Georgia’s pass offense (#4) meets Ole Miss’ pass defense (#38). This gap is not in EdgeDesk’s number: its run-game pairing gets no current-season data. Its matchup term, Georgia +1.1 here, moves through other pairings (across the slate, mostly ball control against front disruption and early-down success). Tested on games it was not fitted on, it helps a little, not yet significantly.

insights.title: HOME FIELD DECIDES IT
insights.short: Ole Miss +2.8 pts for playing at home, more than the projected margin
insights.text: Home field is worth 2.8 points to Ole Miss in EdgeDesk’s projection (the engine’s home-field term). That is more than the projected margin of 2.2: without it, the projection would lean Georgia by 0.6. It is one value for every home team, the same at sea level or at altitude: a per-stadium table was tested and rejected.

insights.title: REGIME CHANGE
insights.short: Ole Miss: new head coach (8 games in).
insights.text: Ole Miss is in a regime change: new head coach; returning roster share at the 28th percentile. The projection weights its long-run rating 60% at 8 games played, the same as any team at this point, so the coaching change adds nothing beyond the team-strength term today. Held-out record of the regime curve: spread MAE −0.032 (95% CI −0.10 to +0.03), better in 7 of 12 seasons.
